newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Up to 100 rebels said killed in Sri Lanka battle.
newsitem.headline: Up to 100 rebels said killed in Sri Lanka battle.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels attacked Sri Lankan navy boats off the island's northeastern coast early on Monday but were repulsed after a four-hour battle, a naval spokesman said.
He said an estimated 100 rebels from the Sea Tigers naval unit of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) were killed and at least 10 rebel boats were sunk when the navy returned fire.

"Some 25-30 rebel boats took us about 10 miles off Mullaitivu after midnight on Sunday. They were met by an equal and strong force from our side and their flotilla was destroyed," the spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said one sailor died and five were wounded in the attack, which began at about 1:45 a.m. (1945 GMT). Mullaitivu lies 280 km (175 miles) from the capital Colombo.
"We have sustained minor damages to our boats," the spokesman said. "Their (the rebels') remaining boats were seen limping back to Mullaitivu."
Other navy officials said 10 rebel boats were destroyed, including two suicide vessels.
"The Tigers had planned to attack a supply convoy that was scheduled to sail today from (the eastern port of) Trincomalee but did not go," said an officer in the area.
An LTTE spokesman in London said he had no immediate details on the battle.

The ethnic Tamil rebels are fighting for a separate homeland in the island's north and east in a civil war now in its 14th year. The government says the war has claimed 50,000 lives but the LTTE says the toll is higher.
Government troops attacked rebel bases in the jungles of Mullaitivu earlier this month. Sea Tiger bases were also attacked.
Military officials said those strikes were aimed at disrupting guerrilla preparations for an attack.
The rebels overran a key military base in the area last year, killing or capturing 1,000 soldiers in the army's worst setback of the war.
